title: The Book of Zephaniah Timeline
sub: The Great Day of the LORD · He Rejoices Over You With Singing
desc: A sweeping oracle of judgment against Judah and the surrounding nations builds to one of the Bible's starkest pictures of the Day of the LORD, before dissolving into one of the most tender images of God's love in all the prophets.

eras.label: Era One · Zephaniah 1
eras.name: The Great Day of the LORD — Silence Before the Judge
eras.dates: A sweeping oracle of coming judgment against Judah and the whole earth, climaxing in one of the Old Testament's starkest descriptions of the Day of the LORD

events.title: I Will Destroy Everything From the Face of the Earth
events.detail: Writing during Josiah's reign, Zephaniah announces a sweeping judgment against Judah's idolatry — Baal worship, star worship, and those who have simply turned their backs on the LORD without seeking his help.

verses.text: “Those who turn their backs on the LORD and do not want the LORD's help or guidance.”

events.title: The Great Day of the LORD Is Almost Here
events.detail: The chapter builds to a thunderous description of the Day of the LORD as a day of wrath, distress, darkness, and trumpet blasts, when neither silver nor gold will be able to save anyone from the LORD's fiery jealousy.

verses.text: “The LORD's [Yahweh's] great day of judgment is almost here; it is approaching very rapidly! There will be a bitter sound on the LORD's [Yahweh's] day of judgment.”
“Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to deliver them in the day of the LORD's [Yahweh's] angry judgment.”

eras.label: Era Two · Zephaniah 2
eras.name: Seek the LORD — Judgment on the Surrounding Nations
eras.dates: A call to repentance opens a chapter that then widens judgment outward to Judah's neighbors on every side

events.title: Seek the LORD, All You Humble People of the Land
events.detail: Before describing judgment on the nations, Zephaniah pauses for an appeal: seek the LORD, strive to do what is right, and perhaps be hidden on the day of his anger.

verses.text: “Seek the LORD's [Yahweh's] favor, all you humble people of the land who have obeyed his commands! Strive to do what is right! Strive to be humble!”

events.title: Judgment on Philistia, Moab, Ammon, Cush, and Assyria
events.detail: Judgment radiates outward to every point of the compass — the Philistine coast, Moab and Ammon compared to Sodom and Gomorrah, Cush struck by the sword, and proud Nineveh reduced to a heap of ruins for wild animals.

verses.text: “This is how the once-proud city will end up—the city that was so secure… What a heap of ruins she has become, a place where wild animals live!”

eras.label: Era Three · Zephaniah 3
eras.name: Judgment on Jerusalem — the LORD Rejoices Over You With Singing
eras.dates: The oracle turns back to Jerusalem's own corruption before closing in one of the most tender promises in the prophets

events.title: The Filthy, Stained City — I Will Purify the Lips of the Peoples
events.detail: Jerusalem's own corrupt leaders — rebellious officials, false prophets, defiling priests — are indicted, followed by a promise that a humble remnant will remain and the nations will be given purified lips to call on the LORD together.

verses.text: “I will then enable the nations to give me acceptable praise. All of them will invoke the LORD's name when they pray and will worship him in unison.”

events.title: The LORD Your God Is in Your Midst — He Rejoices Over You With Singing
events.detail: The book's harsh judgment dissolves into one of Scripture's most affectionate images of God — a warrior-king who delivers, renews his people by his love, and rejoices over them with singing.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] your God [Elohim] is in your midst; he is a warrior who can deliver. He takes great delight in you; he renews you by his love; he shouts for joy over you.”
